subject: Post-call: model fit & prompt collection for ACME - next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@acme.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 23 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: model fit & prompt collection for ACME - next steps

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for a productive call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned: 

1) Key goals we heard from ACME
- High-quality product description generation (customer-facing)
- Short-form ad copy with brand voice constraints
- Sensitive-data redaction for customer PII before storage/eval

2) Immediate model-fit recommendations (initial evals)
- redwood-2-xl (best balance of latency/quality for copy tasks)
- llama3-13b-q8 (cost-effective alternative for bulk generation)
- redwood-code-1 (for structured template rendering where placeholders matter)

3) What we need from your side (ask list) — can you share by EOW: 
- A representative set of prompts (customer-facing examples and known edge cases)
- A small sample of expected outputs (or scoring rubric) so we can benchmark quality
- Any internal redaction rules / fields that must be removed (PII, account ids, product codes)

4) Next steps / timeline
- You upload prompts + redaction guidance to the Drive link below by Thu 8/26
- We’ll run a 3-model eval suite and return a short benchmark + failure-case list by Tue 8/31
- If results look good, we’ll schedule an integration pilot (dedicated capacity or hosted)

Drive link for uploads: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AcmePromptCollectionExample
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345/ACME-2026-07-42

If you’d prefer a template, I can send a CSV template (prompt,input context,expected output,edge-case tags). Otherwise just drop samples in the Drive folder and note any redaction items.

Thanks — looking forward to the prompt set.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0132

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@acme.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: model fit & prompt collection for ACME - next steps

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Attaching a first pass of prompts and our redaction doc. Notes: 

- Attached: acme_prompt_samples.csv (900 rows; a mix of happy-path + some flagged edge cases)
- Attached: redaction_guidance.pdf (internal policy; redacted fields include customer_email, ssn_alt_id, account_internal_id)
- We have a few prompts that include internal product codenames that we’d prefer redacted before leaving our environment.

Quick question: for the scoring rubric, do you want binary accept/reject or a 1–5 subjective quality score? We can provide both, but it will take a bit longer to annotate.

I uploaded both files to the Drive folder and added a short README. Let us know if you need additional context.

Thanks,
Alex Johnson
Product Ops — Acme Corp
alex.johnson@acme.com

Attachments:
- acme_prompt_samples.csv (text/csv, 900 rows)
- redaction_guidance.pdf (application/pdf, internal)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Priya Singh <priya.singh@acme.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: model fit & prompt collection for ACME - next steps

Alex — really helpful, thanks for uploading. I pulled the files and skimmed the README. A few notes and requests so we can run a clean benchmark: 

1) Scoring: a 1–5 subjective quality score + binary accept/reject is ideal. If annotation time is a blocker, send the binary labels and we’ll run subjective scoring internally on a 200-sample subset.

2) Redaction: we can respect your redaction rules. For the pilot evals we have two options: 
   a) Redwood-side preprocessing: you send raw prompts; we apply a redaction pipeline (pattern + allowlist) before storing for evals. We’ll produce a redaction-report for auditing.
   b) Customer-side redaction: you scrub samples and provide already-redacted inputs (preferred by some security teams).

Please confirm which you prefer. Note: option (a) lets us run tests closer to your production signal if you’re comfortable. Either way, we’ll make sure any PII is excluded from logs per our data retention policy.

3) Edge cases: I noticed several prompts that reference internal codename \"NEPTUNE\" and some that contain multi-field address-like strings. Can you flag the NEPTUNE prompts as internal-only so we exclude them from public eval examples?

4) Model/baseline plan (what we’ll run this week):
- redwood-2-xl: primary baseline (expected best human-like copy quality)
- llama3-13b-q8: cost baseline for throughput tests
- redwood-code-1: template rendering correctness on structured prompts

We’ll also run simple regression checks vs. your provided expected outputs and surface top failure modes (hallucination, truncation, tokenization issues).

ETA: assuming prompt set is finalized, we’ll have a first-pass benchmark and failure-case write-up by Tue 8/31. If you prefer earlier, we can prioritize a 200-row quick run and share preliminary results by Fri 8/27.

I’ve added the HubSpot deal and noted ACME-2026-07-42. A couple small asks: if you can mark which prompts are edge cases vs. core traffic and include any business scoring rules, that will speed evaluation.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AcmePromptCollectionExample
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345/ACME-2026-07-42

Thanks — I’ll loop in Ben and Logan to run the evals once we have confirmation on redaction approach.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: model fit & prompt collection for ACME - next steps

Thanks for the upload, Alex — and thanks Marissa for the plan. Quick internal note / confirmation: 

- We’ll run the three-model suite (redwood-2-xl, llama3-13b-q8, redwood-code-1) and produce the regression/quality report. Ben will own the redaction audit and produce the redaction-report if ACME chooses Redwood-side preprocessing.
- Tentative ETA for the full benchmark: Tue 2026-08-31 (deliverable: benchmark CSV + short write-up + top 10 failure cases).
- Quick-run option (200 rows) available by Fri 2026-08-27 if ACME wants earlier visibility.

Ben — can you confirm you’re OK to run the redaction audit if they choose option (a)? I’ll also pull legal if we need an MSA addendum for redaction processing.

Alex / Priya — let us know which redaction option you want. If you want us to proceed with option (a), we’ll need an explicit scope of fields to redact (the PDF looked like a good start).

- Logan
Logan Wright
Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
logan_wright@redwood.ai
